newsitem.title: UK: Grain freight trade in London busy before holidays.
newsitem.headline: Grain freight trade in London busy before holidays.

text.p: Brokers reported firm conditions in most areas of the dry cargo market, despite Friday's unchanged Baltic Freight Index, anchored at 1,523.
There were encouraging signs for owners with the completion of a number of period timecharter deals and a healthy level of fresh grain enquiry from North and South America and Australia.
Panamax rates in the North Pacific appeared steadier after looking a little shaky in recent days, brokers said.
They also reported a shortage of handy tonnage in the US Gulf and Argentina.
Grain business was described as brisk.

Brokers said Cobelfret booked Orleta Lwowskie for 56,000 tonnes heavy grain US Gulf/Ghent for January 10-20 at $14.25, generally considered steady for a forward position but down from the $14.90 paid by Cargill earlier this week for Maratha Majesty for 63,000 tonnes US Gulf/Netherlands for end December.
The 1976-built Ermioni 66,157 dwt was reported fixed by RAC delivery spot US Gulf for a trip via Aqaba redelivery Passero at $9,500 plus $200,000-250,000 bonus but failed on subjects.

Continental were said to be willing to relet 54,000 tonnes heavy grain US Gulf/Japan for January 16-28 at $26.25 with combo without finding any takers. Bobilna 64,854 dwt was reported booked for delivery prompt Flushing for a trip Far East at $13,000 daily, but details were unavailable.
Fresh enquiry included Bluedeck with 50,000 tonnes wheat US Gulf/Egypt for 1-15 January and Toepfer with 75,000 tonnes barley Rouen and Dunkirk/Saudi Arabia for January 4-10.
Panamaxes were in demand for grain trips in the East.

Continental were said to have covered 54,000 tonnes heavy grains Nopac/Japan on subjects and Nephele 71,927 dwt was reported booked on private terms by Toepfer for Nopac/Saudi business. Emirates Trading also covered a Panamax privately on timecharter for grain from Australia to Jebel Ali.
Transchart were active with fixtures of four shipments of 55,000 tonnes wheat western Australia/Nhava Sheva for Jan-March at $16.75, option loading South or East for a dollar more.

Handies were also in demand for grain from Australia, account Transchart, for up to 40,000/5 tonnes wheat prompt/onwards, the Australian Wheat Board for 30,000 tonnes Australia/Nigeria also prompt, and Glencore early January 30,000 tonnes barley Victoria in South Australia to China.
Handies continued to obtain firm rates from the Plate.

Continental was said to have fixed Olympia 27,306 dwt delivery Recalada for a trip to the Med on private terms and another over-age vessel of similar size was reported fixed from the Plate for a trip to East Africa, said to be at a hefty rate.

Bluedeck were reported to have fixed two Handies US Gulf/Egypt but details on only one were available - a 28,000 dwt modern vessel with December delivery to the South-West Pass at a firmer $8,000 daily plus $100,000 bonus redelivery Egypt.
A parcel of 25,000/10 tonnes wheat US Gulf/Algeria was reported booked for the second half of January at $20.40.

New handy orders quoted included Dreyfus 25,000 tonnes heavy grain US Gulf/Malaysia for Jan 1-15 and 32,000-40,000 tonnes Mississippi/Lisbon-Hamburg range for Jan 4-10, Continental 30-45,000 tonnes US Gulf/Lisbon-Denmark range for Dec/Jan, Argentine Wheat Board for 25,000 T wheat Upriver/Malaysia for 5-15 Jan and Comshipco 26-29,000 T Paranagua/Weser for 8-18 Jan.
In mineral trades, brokers said Klaveness failed on subjects with Marine Courage for 125,000 T ironore Tubarao/China for Jan 15-30. One broker said Caper orders seemed to be drying up in the East.
Pan Ocean were said to have booked Hanjin Tacoma 70,457 dwt delivery Hong Kong next week for 3-5 months redelivery Far East at $11,300 daily, first leg said Richards Bay/Le Havre for coal.
Shinwa were linked with a 70,000 dwt vessel, possibly Pasquale Della Gatta, delivery Japan in early January for three to five months, but there were no further details.

Handy trades included two newbuildings reported fixed in the East - K Silver 44,000 dwt ex yard S.Korea for 12 months to Shinwa at close to $9,000 daily and Pacific Scorpio 45,000 dwt ex yard Nagasaki early Jan for 1-2 years in the low $9,000s.

On the Continent, Cargo Levant reportedly fixed a 28,000 dwt vessel to India, Van Ommeren a 31,000 dwt craned bulker to US Gulf at $6,200 daily and UBT a gearless 35,000 dwt from Baltic to US Gulf on subjects at $5,600 daily. --London Newsroom, +44 171 542 8071
